formNote: Mojidata IDS: ⿰亻二. The Shuowen: 仁，親也。从人从二 — “closeness: from person and two.” A virtue that exists only between people.
summary: Humaneness, the central Confucian virtue: graphically a person and two, a virtue that only exists between people. Asked what it is, Confucius said 愛人, “to love people”; Mencius said it simply is being human.
placement: At the fixed point at the centre of the Rössler spiral (x ≈ 0.007, y ≈ −0.035, z ≈ 0.035), which the disk winds around: humaneness, the root the other virtues turn on. (Placement is a design choice, not a claim.)

oc.note: † Baracus, from general knowledge; not yet checked against B–S 2014.

satellites.title: Humaneness Named After the Human
satellites.evidence: 仁 is written with 人, “person”, and Mencius says 仁也者，人也: humaneness simply is being human (and, joined together, the two are the Way). Malay builds its word the same way, perikemanusiaan from manusia, “human being”, and Latin humanitas grows from homo, as English humane does from human.
satellites.caveat: Parallel word-building, not shared ancestry or shared doctrine. Roman humanitas also meant refinement and learning, and perikemanusiaan is a modern civic word. 仁’s closeness between two people (从人从二) has no counterpart in either.

satellites.title: Humaneness Is Loving People
satellites.evidence: Analects 12.22: 樊遲問仁。子曰：愛人 — Fan Chi asks about 仁, and the answer is two characters: “love people.”

satellites.title: Mastering Oneself, Returning to the Rites
satellites.evidence: Analects 12.1: 克己復禮為仁 — “to master oneself and return to the rites is humaneness.” Here 仁 is reached through 禮.
satellites.caveat: The reading of 克己 (“overcome the self” or “discipline oneself”) is debated.
